parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; Probably; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: each of the coils of a rope; a fake
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin. Probably from Genoese Ligurian duggia (compare with Italian duglia (“a coil, a fake”), ultimately from Latin dūpla. First attested in 1842.
Borrowed from Ligurian anciôa, from Vulgar Latin *apiuva, from Latin aphyē (“small fry”), from Ancient Greek ἀφύη (aphúē). Doublet of anjova.

parole.significato: mob (rude or vulgar group of people)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian ciüsma (from which Italian ciurma and Portuguese chusma descend), from Latin celeusma, from Ancient Greek κέλευσμα (kéleusma, “rhythmic chant to exhort rowers in galleys”), from κελεύω (keleúō, “to order, to bid, to exhort”). Doublet of saloma.
